quiz.q: Glide ratio equals…
quiz.why: Distance over height = L/D.

quiz.q: Power required in level flight is…
quiz.why: Drag times speed.

quiz.q: Breguet range grows with…
quiz.why: R ∝ L/D.

quiz.q: Climb comes from…
quiz.why: RC = excess power/W.

quiz.q: A heavier glider glides farther.
quiz.why: Glide ratio depends on L/D, not weight; weight changes the best speed.

quiz.q: Range depends only on the fuel load.
quiz.why: It depends on engine efficiency, L/D and the weight fraction (Breguet).

quiz.q: Flying faster always gives more range.
quiz.why: Best range comes at a moderate speed tied to the best L/D.

quiz.q: A sailplane with L/D = 20 is 1,000 m up. How far can it glide in still air, and at what angle? Give your answer in km.
quiz.why: 20 km, at a glide angle of about 2.9°.

quiz.q: A jet cruises at 230 m/s with L/D = 17 and thrust-specific fuel consumption c = 0.6 per hour. Burning fuel lowers its weight from W_i to W_i/1.25. Find its range. Give your answer in km.
The Example 3.1 airplane, with the Example 4.3 drag polar, has about 957 N of drag at 55 m/s. What power does level flight require? Give your answer in kW.
quiz.why: ≈ 52.6 kW (about 71 hp).

quiz.q: A paper glider has L/D = 5. Launched level from 2 m, about how far does it glide?
An aircraft weighing 10,800 N has 30 kW of excess power. Find its rate of climb. Give your answer in m/s.
In Example 5.2, how does range change if L/D rises from 17 to 20? Give your answer in km.
How far can the Example 4.3 airplane glide from 1,500 m at its best L/D of 13.7? Give your answer in km.

The Breguet equation is aviation’s climate equation: for a given trip, fuel burned falls when engines get more efficient, wings get higher L/D, or structures get lighter. With the other terms fixed, range is proportional to L/D.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: NASA estimates that with today’s fleet and operations, worldwide air traffic in 2050 would need more than 620 million tonnes of fuel and emit close to 2,000 million tonnes of CO₂, which is why every term in the equation matters.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: A glider with lift-to-drag ratio L/D travels L/D meters forward for every meter of height lost: tan γ = D/L.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: Thrust required in level flight equals drag; power required is drag × speed. Excess power becomes climb: rate of climb = (P_avail − P_req)/W.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: For a jet, range follows the Breguet equation: R = (V/c)(L/D) ln(W_i/W_f). Three levers: engine efficiency (V/c), aerodynamics (L/D) and structures (weight fraction).
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: Endurance (time aloft) is maximized at a different speed than range.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.
